nodes.label: AesGcmPayloadCipher (id aesgcm)
nodes.source_location: ## Real encryption out of the box: AES-GCM (recommended)
nodes.rationale: AES-GCM authenticated encryption with a random IV per write and a 128-bit tag, auto-registered when failover.store.jdbc.encryption.key is non-empty; an invalid key fails startup fast. Being authenticated it throws on a tampered row or wrong key rather than returning corrupted data.

nodes.label: Cipher / key rotation procedure
nodes.rationale: Because each row records its cipher id, rotation is rolling: add the new cipher alongside the old, point writes at it, let old rows decrypt via the retained bean, drop the old bean once they expire. A row naming an unregistered cipher throws FailoverStoreException, which is acceptable because the store is a disposable cache.

nodes.label: Encryption operational notes (column sizing, lookups, key secrecy)
nodes.rationale: Ciphertext is larger than plaintext so PAYLOAD must be sized up. Lookups are unaffected because the store key is FAILOVER_NAME + FAILOVER_KEY, not the payload, so a random-IV ciphertext does not break find. The key must come from a secret manager; losing it only costs a cold start since the store is regenerable.
